problem_statement: The flash simulator does not support registering custom callbacks for write and erase operations. A testing framework needs to inject failures or corrupt data during flash write and erase operations (e.g., to simulate broken flash memory that returns errors or corrupts data on certain pages) without modifying the driver. The expected behavior is: a user can register a write-byte callback that can return a modified byte value or an error code during flash write, and an erase-unit callback that can return an error code or perform custom erase logic during flash erase. The user can also retrieve flash simulator parameters (erase unit size, erase value, etc.) to determine which page an offset falls on. Before this change, these functions and types do not exist, so any code using them fails to build.

verification.reason: The hidden code relies on exact Kconfig, header, struct, field, function, and callback semantics that the original statement does not specify; these can be added without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The statement does not give the exact names required by the code: CONFIG_FLASH_SIMULATOR_CALLBACKS, flash_simulator_cb, write_byte, erase_unit, flash_simulator_set_callbacks, flash_simulator_params, flash_simulator_get_params, and the field erase_value.
The configuration must expose CONFIG_FLASH_SIMULATOR_CALLBACKS, but the statement only says functions and types are missing without naming the Kconfig option.

The required public behavior is under-specified: the write callback is per byte with the absolute byte offset, the erase callback is per erase unit with the unit start offset, a set erase callback replaces the default erase, NULL clears callbacks, and negative callback returns propagate as flash_write or flash_erase errors.
The new API must be available from the flash simulator public header and must expose the named structures and functions with the expected field and parameter names.

problem_statement_fixed: The flash simulator does not support registering custom callbacks for write and erase operations. A testing framework needs to inject failures or corrupt data during flash write and erase operations (e.g., to simulate broken flash memory that returns errors or corrupts data on certain pages) without modifying the driver. The expected behavior is: a user can register a write-byte callback that can return a modified byte value or an error code during flash write, and an erase-unit callback that can return an error code or perform custom erase logic during flash erase. The user can also retrieve flash simulator parameters (erase unit size, erase value, etc.) to determine which page an offset falls on. Before this change, these functions and types do not exist, so any code using them fails to build. The callback feature is enabled by CONFIG_FLASH_SIMULATOR_CALLBACKS. When this option is enabled, the public API shall be available from <zephyr/drivers/flash/flash_simulator.h>. flash_simulator_set_callbacks(const struct device *dev, const struct flash_simulator_cb *cb) shall register the callback structure for the flash simulator device; passing NULL shall clear registered callbacks. The callback structure shall be named flash_simulator_cb and shall contain fields write_byte and erase_unit. The write-byte callback shall be invoked for each byte during a flash write and shall have signature int (*)(const struct device *dev, off_t offset, uint8_t data); its non-negative return value is the byte to be stored at offset, and a negative return value shall abort the flash write and be returned as the write error. The erase-unit callback shall be invoked for each erase unit during a flash erase and shall have signature int (*)(const struct device *dev, off_t unit_offset); 0 is success and a negative return value shall abort the flash erase and be returned as the erase error. When an erase-unit callback is registered, it shall be responsible for performing the erase, and the flash simulator shall not additionally perform its own erase for that unit. flash_simulator_get_params(const struct device *dev) shall return a const struct flash_simulator_params * containing the flash simulator parameters; when CONFIG_FLASH_SIMULATOR_CALLBACKS is enabled, it shall return a valid pointer. The parameters structure shall be named flash_simulator_params and shall include fields named erase_unit and erase_value, corresponding to the erase unit size and the erased byte value.
